claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
An aluminum addition of approximately 2–3 at% is an appropriate intervention for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Adding 2–3 at% Al will promote formation of a continuous alumina surface scale during exposure in air at 800 °C.
The alumina scale will be adherent and protective.
Added aluminum preferentially oxidizes to Al2O3 at the alloy surface.
The resulting alumina scale is stable and slow-growing.
The alumina scale restricts oxygen penetration into the bulk alloy.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, the Al-modified alloy will have significantly lower oxidation weight gain than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, the Al-modified alloy will have a thinner oxide layer than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al-modified alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance under similar high-temperature conditions.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation, deleterious scaling, and loss of mechanical performance under similar high-temperature conditions.
The predicted benefit is bounded to 2–3 at% Al, 800 °C air exposure for 5 hours, and mechanical testing at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The oxidation and mechanical benefits depend on the Al addition not significantly altering the alloy microstructure.
The optimum aluminum concentration and oxidation improvement may depend on processing parameters and minor composition variations.
